context.attribution: Consortium for Grid Integrity — Industry group, US
context.text: A regulatory surplus test means something different in a market with a binding clean energy standard than in one without. The same test, applied globally, will not measure the same thing twice.

against.text: The proposed formula assumes a counterfactual dispatch that no reporting entity can observe, let alone have assured. We would be asking auditors to sign off on a model output, not a measurement.

context.text: We are not opposed to the direction. We are saying the draft is underspecified in exactly the places where two good-faith preparers would reach different numbers.

for.text: Inventory accounting tells us who owns an emission; it says nothing about whether the purchase changed what the system dispatched. […] A consequential layer is the only way to make that question answerable at all.
